subject.title: RFC: Org claim disputes and account recovery

question: What permanent authorization and disclosure contract should ClawHub use for disputed namespaces and recovery after owner-initiated deletion?
rationale: Source code can implement a chosen rule, but it cannot determine which identity evidence is sufficient, whether deletion forfeits namespace rights, what may be disclosed publicly, or which security and moderation states permanently block recovery.

options.title: Define bounded recovery policy
options.body: Publish a policy allowing verified claims and eligible self-deletion recovery through audited staff review while keeping bans, abuse actions, competing claims, and sensitive evidence on a separate private path.

options.title: Keep discretionary staff review
options.body: Document only the intake channels and leave evidence thresholds, namespace disposition, and recovery scope to unpublished case-by-case staff judgment.

options.title: Make deletion final
options.body: Declare owner-initiated deletion permanently non-recoverable and release or reserve associated namespaces under a separately documented fixed rule.

recommendation.title: Define bounded recovery policy
recommendation.body: Publish a policy allowing verified claims and eligible self-deletion recovery through audited staff review while keeping bans, abuse actions, competing claims, and sensitive evidence on a separate private path.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the RFC and the merged public namespace-claim intake work, giving them the strongest available continuity for coordinating the final policy decision.
